marks.gloss_en: plain thought he does not ask about; he asks where the minor's thought is discernible from his actions
e.g. a burnt-offering stood in the south, he brought it to the north and slaughtered it: since he brought it north, did he intend it [as a burnt-offering]?
one who takes his produce up to the roof against vermin and dew fell on it -- it is not in [the category of] 'ki yutan' (Lev 11:38)
if a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor took them up, even if they intended it -- it is not in 'ki yutan'
R' Yochanan: they taught this only where he did not turn them over
this is what he asks: [is it effective] by Torah law or by rabbinic law? (the object -- thought discernible from action -- is supplied by the preceding exchange)
version 2, horn 1: does a minor have [halakhically effective] action?
version 2: this is what he asks: [are the minor's capacities as the mishna states them] by Torah law or by rabbinic law?
one acting unawares (mitasek) in [slaughtering] sacrifices -- [the offering] is disqualified
נבלה אין, איסור הנאה לא -- the mishna says 'carcass' and not 'forbidden for benefit'
דאי רבי אליעזר, האמר: סתם מחשבת נכרי לעבודה זרה -- for R' Eliezer the gentile's slaughter would be forbidden for benefit
a carcass -- yes; forbidden for benefit -- no
תנינא להא דתנו רבנן: שחיטת מין לעבודה זרה (no support kind names תנינא; dika_nami is the nearest -- learned by inference from the mishna)
R' Ami: this is what it teaches -- a gentile's slaughter is a carcass; but a heretic's is for idol worship
a gentile's slaughter [renders the animal] a carcass
